newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez, Lyonnaise no comment on merge talk.
newsitem.headline: Suez, Lyonnaise no comment on merge talk.

text.p: French holding company Cie de Suez and utilities company Lyonnaise des Eaux declined comment on Monday on a weekend report in Le Monde that their chairmen were working together to conclude a merger proposal.
Le Monde, citing unnamed sources, said the two chairmen wanted to make rapid progress in working on a proposed merger ahead of a Suez board meeting on April 1.
"We have no comment," a Suez spokeswoman said.
"We have absolutely nothing to say on this," a Lyonnaise spokeswoman said.
A spokeswoman for glassmaker Saint Gobain, whose chairman was reported by Le Monde to be involved in discussions, said the company had no comment.
Saint-Gobain holds six percent of Suez's capital and 10 percent of the voting rights.
Financial weekly Investir on Friday reported that Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) was considering a hostile bid for Suez to block a merger between Suez and its rival Lyonnaise.
But a source close to the group said on Friday that CGE's strategy was not an acquisition of Suez.
